items.rationale: Frost fracture of an internal fitting is covered under 2.4.3(b) and 7.1.9, like for like. Ordinary price for a filling valve, sized so the plumbing lines total about EUR 450 as in reference case 7.
Connection elements renewed with the fractured fitting are covered under 2.4.3 and 7.1.9. Small material item at ordinary price.
Labour for the covered fitting renewal is indemnified under 7.1.9. Three hours at about EUR 70 gross, consistent with the roughly EUR 450 total in reference case 7.
Consumables actually used in covered work are indemnified under 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.9. Small flat rate.
One attendance per undertaking is indemnified under 7.1.11 and 7.1.9 because covered work was carried out at it. Modest call-out charge.
Leak location with imaging equipment is covered under 2.4.5 and 5.2.2, and the EUR 2,500 cap is far from reached. Ordinary flat rate for thermal imaging.
Frost damage to an external surface is excluded under 3.1.4(b) and 3.5(a), so it is not an affected part (7.1.5). Reference case 7 gave t = 0 for the facade.
Taking off loosened surface material on the facade is excluded under 3.5(b).
Re-forming the substrate of the external surface is excluded under 3.5(b).
Further work on the elevation on the same occasion is excluded under 3.5(b), and it cannot be allocated to a part damaged by an insured event (9.6).
Preparation and levelling of the facade substrate is excluded under 3.5(b) and 7.1.7 last paragraph.
Successive coats of the new finish on an external surface are excluded under 3.5(b), however many are applied.
Drying out the facade substrate is excluded under 3.5(b). Drying under 7.1.7(c) exists only for an affected part.
Priming of the external surface is excluded under 3.5(b).
Labour on excluded facade work is an ancillary charge excluded under 3.5(c) and 7.1.11. The plumber's covered work does not carry the painter's account (7.1.12).
A lump sum in respect of excluded facade work is excluded under 3.5(c). A general flat rate is also not a repair cost under 7.1.8(b).
